name: Command Desk
tag: Three columns: your day, the inbox, the numbers
why: Left rail for the 8 tabs. Column one is the phone Today screen (Now card, steps, run sheet, Film Mode) so nothing you learned changes. Column two is the Approve inbox, live on the home screen with Send, Copy, Edit, Skip, so you answer DMs without leaving Home. Column three is every number: money bar, deal stages, content flow, week scoreboard, waiting counts. One screen, no tabs, for a big monitor.

name: Inbox Desk
tag: Mail style: list on the left, the draft big in the middle, your day on the right
why: Built around answering. The left pane lists every waiting message like Superhuman: name, channel, hot badge, time. The middle shows the selected draft large with context above it, Send, Copy, Edit, Skip below, and J/K to move. The right rail keeps the Now card, up next, money bar, deals due today and the week. Fastest for a 20-DM session on the Mac, and Copy sits right under the draft for iMessage leads.

name: Board Desk
tag: One wide board: pipelines as columns, the day as a timeline, every number on top
why: Top bar instead of a rail so the board gets the full width. A KPI strip runs across the top: money bar, four week targets, five waiting counts. Under it the Deal pipeline and Content pipeline as real Kanban columns, each card with the next step and due date, which is where the four desks write. The day runs along the bottom as a horizontal timeline with the Now card, and Film Mode and the Idea box sit next to it. The most information per screen, built for a 27 inch monitor.
